Executive Summary

The chai-com workload exhibits a compounded risk profile within the multi-tenant cluster. Application-level vulnerabilities (DOM XSS, SSRF) act as direct stepping stones to critical cluster infrastructure due to a lack of network isolation and overly permissive cloud IAM roles. An unauthenticated external attacker can achieve full cloud account takeover in a single attack chain.

🚨 Top 3 Immediate Remediation Priorities

1. Block the SSRF to IMDS Escalation [DevOps] + [AppSec]
If ignored: Any vulnerability in the app code allows attackers to pull Cloud IAM credentials directly from the node.
2. Lock Down the Node IAM Role (s3:*) [CloudSec]
If ignored: A compromised pod instantly has read/write access to all S3 buckets in the cloud account (2.1M PII records exposed).
3. Remove Kubelet Anonymous Auth [SecOps / Platform]
If ignored: Anyone inside the VPC can execute commands (kubelet exec) in any pod, skipping Kubernetes RBAC entirely.

Scope & Methodology

This threat model evaluates the chai-com service, its supporting Kubernetes platform, and the connected cloud account. The assessment follows a hybrid methodology combining STRIDE, PASTA, and MITRE ATT&CK for Containers. It is driven by a 26-agent static and dynamic scanning pipeline, with AI correlation deduplicating findings.

In Scope

  • chai-com application source (Node.js / Express + Angular SPA)
  • Helm chart and Kubernetes manifests for chai-com
  • Terraform modules provisioning the EKS cluster and node groups
  • Kubernetes cluster control plane (kube-apiserver, kubelet, etcd)
  • CI/CD pipeline (GitHub Actions) used to deploy chai-com
  • Cloud IAM roles attached to nodes, pods (IRSA), and CI
  • Data flows involving PII, PCI, and JWT secrets

Out of Scope

  • Third-party SaaS dependencies beyond identity providers
  • Physical datacenter controls and underlying cloud hardware
  • Corporate endpoint (developer laptop) EDR coverage
  • Customer browser security beyond CSP enforcement
  • Social engineering and phishing vectors

Assumptions & Dependencies

Trusted Platform Assumption

The cloud provider's substrate (hypervisor, hardware) is trusted. Escape from the provider's trust boundary is out of scope.

Identity Provider Assumption

The external IdP used to mint JWTs is correctly configured. Only JWT signing material held inside chai-com is in scope.

Network Reachability Assumption

Pod egress can reach 169.254.169.254 unless explicitly blocked. NetworkPolicy is enforced by a compatible CNI.

Environment Parity Assumption

The staging cluster used for Red Team replay is a faithful clone of production. Config drift invalidates validation timing.

Pipeline Execution Findings

Agent Severity Finding & Threat Details, PoC & Impact
01. Context Ingestion: Design & PRD Review
Design ReviewHIGH Missing Auth Rotation Authentication relies on a single HS256 JWT without rotation.
Impact: Long-term persistence if key is leaked.
Design ReviewHIGH Missing Namespace Boundary No defined trust boundary between the workload namespace and kube-system.
Impact: Lateral movement across tenant boundaries.
02. Code Analysis
SAST AgentCRIT SQL Injection (Auth Bypass)
T1190		 Constructs queries via string concatenation in routes/search.ts.
PoC: POST /rest/user/login {"email":"' OR 1=1--"}
Impact: Full database dump including PII/PCI.
SAST AgentCRIT Server-Side Request Forgery
T1552.005		 Unvalidated URL parameter in routes/profileImageUrl.ts allows internal network probing.
Impact: Access to internal APIs and Cloud Metadata.
Secrets AgentCRIT Committed Cloud Creds
T1552.001		 Active AWS Access Key ID committed in .env.example.
Impact: Instant cloud account compromise.
🧠 AI ENGINE: MULTI-AGENT CORRELATION

Correlation & Validation: Code Scanning

The AI engine merged the SAST SSRF finding and the committed AWS Key into a verified application-layer exploit chain.

SRE Runbook: Immediate Remediation

  • Revoke Keys: In AWS IAM Console, revoke the compromised Access Key immediately.
  • Fix SSRF: In routes/profileImageUrl.ts, implement an allowed domain list.
03. IaC & Pipeline
TerraformCRIT IMDSv1 Enabled on Node
T1552.005		 EKS node group allows IMDSv1 queries without a session token.
PoC: fetch('http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/')
Impact: Pods with SSRF can extract Node IAM credentials.
HelmCRIT Privileged Container Escape
T1611		 Deployment runs the container with privileged: true and hostPID: true.
PoC: nsenter --target 1 --mount --uts --ipc --net --pid
Impact: Container escape to underlying worker node as root.
🧠 AI ENGINE: MULTI-AGENT CORRELATION

Correlation & Validation: Code + Infra

Mapped the application-layer SSRF directly to the Terraform-provisioned IMDSv1 nodes, confirming an escalation path to Cloud IAM.

SRE Runbook: Immediate Remediation

  • Patch Manifest: In helm/charts/.../deployment.yaml, set privileged: false.
  • Enforce IMDSv2: In terraform/eks-nodes.tf, set http_tokens = "required".
04. Cloud & Cluster Posture
Cloud ConfigCRIT Over-Permissive IAM
T1078.004		 IAM role attached to worker nodes possesses s3:* wildcard permissions.
Impact: Broad data exfiltration from any compromised node.
K8s SecurityCRIT Unauth Kubelet API
T1609		 The Kubelet allows anonymous-auth on port 10250, bypassing RBAC.
Impact: Remote Code Execution in any cluster pod.
🧠 AI ENGINE: MULTI-AGENT CORRELATION

Correlation & Validation: Cloud Posture

Connecting the permissive Node IAM role to the unauth kubelet verified that node compromise equals total cloud account and cluster compromise.

SRE Runbook: Immediate Remediation

  • Lock Kubelet: Edit /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml on nodes: set authentication.anonymous.enabled: false.
  • Restrict IAM: In terraform/iam.tf, replace s3:* with a scoped policy.
05 & 06. Defense & Paved Path
StandardsHIGH Missing Network Isolation
T1021		 No default-deny NetworkPolicy exists. East-west traffic is unrestricted.
Impact: Seamless lateral movement for attackers.
Product Def.HIGH Missing CSP Header
T1059.007		 No Content-Security-Policy header is emitted.
Impact: Silent session hijacking via XSS payloads.
🧠 AI ENGINE: MULTI-AGENT CORRELATION

Correlation & Validation: Defense Deficiencies

The lack of NetworkPolicies combined with the lack of CSP means attackers face zero friction traversing from the browser to the backend network.

SRE Runbook: Immediate Remediation

  • Isolate Network: Create k8s/network-policy.yaml with DefaultDeny.
  • Add Header: In server.ts, append Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'.
07. Validation & Attack Path Analysis

The Red Team agent utilized the aggregated pipeline findings to autonomously execute CHN-KILL-01 in the staging environment. Total time to cluster-admin was 2 hours and 47 minutes.

Primary Attack Path — CHN-KILL-01
Validation Status: FULLY_VALIDATED (Red Team, stage)

│ HTTP GET /#/search?q=<script>
▼
[ALB - ingress] <- Missing CSP

│-> fetch('http://169.254.169.254/...')
▼

│-> RETURNS: AWS AccessKeyId
▼
[Cloud IAM - node-role] <- s3:* Wildcard
│-> SELECT / DUMP -> 2.1M PII records
│-> kube-system exec -> Cluster-admin
Red Team execution trace (2026-04-15): XSS achieved → Admin JWT stolen → SSRF directed to IMDS → Node IAM credentials extracted → S3 data buckets dumped → Cluster-admin pod exec achieved.
